name: Dental medication review blocks incomplete context and abstains with an empty approved catalog
covers: no autonomous medication selection or prescription
description: Verifies the core dental medication-review workflow requires dentist-confirmed context and never invents medication suggestions when no pathway is approved.
steps: Open Medication review from the workspace navigation.
Submit the form with all fields empty.
Verify the review is blocked and lists missing diagnosis, dentist confirmation, age, allergies, medicines, pregnancy/lactation context, organ-function context and local protocol.

Enter fictional data: diagnosis code DEMO-DENT-001, diagnosis label Synthetic dental scenario, age 35, allergies 'none reported and confirmed (synthetic)', and current medicines 'none reported and confirmed (synthetic)'.

Confirm the diagnosis, allergy review, medication reconciliation and local protocol review; set pregnancy/lactation to clinician-confirmed not applicable and renal/hepatic status to clinician-confirmed not applicable.
Select Review approved pathways.
expected: The app shows zero approved pathways and returns no medication candidate or dose. It says the empty catalog is not advice to withhold treatment, displays teaching-card requirements, and preserves the clinician’s responsibility.

name: Clinical-trials research builder creates independent public source links
covers: research records are not prescribing approval
description: Verifies search terms produce separate trial and literature links without fetching data into or creating a medicine-ranking system.
steps: Open Trials & research.
Enter 'synthetic dental pain' as the condition and 'fictional test intervention' as the intervention; keep Egypt selected.
Click Build source searches.
Verify ClinicalTrials.gov, WHO ICTRP, PubMed, DailyMed, LactMed and ADA guideline links appear.
Open ClinicalTrials.gov in a new tab and verify the search includes Egypt as the location.
Verify the safety note says a trial record is not treatment authorization.
expected: Distinct public source links are displayed for the synthetic topic and intervention; ClinicalTrials.gov is Egypt-focused, and research discovery is separated from medication decisions. No patient details are submitted.

name: Research builder rejects an empty query and safely renders research text on mobile
covers: safe text rendering for search terms
description: Verifies a missing topic produces a clear error and a phrase containing markup is rendered as text instead of executing.
steps: Open Trials & research on a mobile viewport.
Click Build source searches without entering a condition or intervention.
Verify a message asks for a non-identifying topic or medicine name and no source result cards are shown.
Enter '<script>synthetic test</script>' as the condition and submit.
Verify the query appears as text in the page heading and no script popup executes.
expected: Empty searches show a visible validation message. Search terms render as escaped text, and the app does not store the query or make automatic network calls.

name: Information centers show official dental guidance and Egyptian medicine-safety contacts
covers: Egyptian Drug Authority Drug Information Center
description: Verifies the reference directory exposes source-linked guidance and warns that US references do not establish Egyptian product authorization.
steps: Open Information centers.
Verify ADA acute pain, ADA antibiotic stewardship, DailyMed, LactMed, WHO ICTRP and Egyptian Drug Authority entries are visible.
Verify the EDA Drug Information Center phone and email are visible.
Verify the page warns that US labeling does not establish Egyptian registration or local prescribing rules.
expected: The page shows official source links, EDA contact details and jurisdiction limits. Source discovery alone does not produce a medication recommendation.
